items.from_text: Why do you gaze in envy, O mountains of many peaks? This is the mountain God chose for His dwelling, where the LORD will surely dwell forever.
items.to_text: In the last days the mountain of the house of the LORD will be established as the chief of the mountains; it will be raised above the hills, and all nations will stream to it.

original_justification: 1 Kgs 8:6/2 Sam 6:17 show the ark being brought into and housed within the tabernacle — a furnishing, not a coordinate structure.

a.label: Ark
a.definition: Noah’s ark, a building of gopher-wood, and covered with pitch, 300 cubits long, 50 cubits broad, and 30 cubits high ([Gen. 6:14-16](/gen#Gen.6.14)); an oblong floating house of three stories, with a door in the side and a window in the roof. original_justification: Judg 4:3/Josh 17:16 name iron as the reinforcing material of chariots ('chariots of iron').

a.label: Chariot
a.definition:

b.definition: Tubal-Cain is the first-mentioned worker in iron ([Gen. 4:22](/gen#Gen.4.22)). The Egyptians wrought it at Sinai before the Exodus. original_justification: Exod 16:10 and Easton's own Shechinah entry ('he went before them in a pillar of a cloud... the symbol of his presence') establish the cloud as the visible form the Shechinah took.

a.label: Cloud
a.definition: The Hebrew so rendered means “a covering,” because clouds cover the sky. The word is used as a symbol of the Divine presence, as indicating the splendour of that glory which it conceals ([Ex. 16:10](/exod#Exod.16.10); [33:9](/exod#Exod.33.9); [Num. 11:25](/num#Num.11.25); [12:5](/num#Num.12.5); [Job 22:14](/job#Job.22.14); [Ps. 18:11](/ps#Ps.18.11)). b.label: Shechinah
b.definition: A Chaldee word meaning resting-place, not found in Scripture, but used by the later Jews to designate the visible symbol of God’s presence in the tabernacle, and afterwards in Solomon’s temple. When the Lord led Israel out of Egypt, he went before them “in a pillar of a cloud.” This was the symbol of his presence with his people. original_justification: Gen 16:2 (Sarai's barrenness as a divine restraint) and Ps 127:3 (children as a heritage/blessing) frame barrenness and having a child as the two poles of a real theological reproach/blessing opposition — the clearest genuine antonym pair in this batch.

a.label: Barren
a.definition: For a woman to be barren was accounted a severe punishment among the Jews ([Gen. 16:2](/gen#Gen.16.2); [30:1-23](/gen#Gen.30.1); [1 Sam. 1:6](/1sam#1Sam.1.6), [27](/1sam#1Sam.1.27); [Isa. 47:9](/isa#Isa.47.9); [49:21](/isa#Isa.49.21); [Luke 1:25](/luke#Luke.1.25)). b.label: Child
b.definition:
This word has considerable latitude of meaning in Scripture. Thus Joseph is called a child at the time when he was probably about sixteen years of age ([Gen. 37:3](/gen#Gen.37.3)); and Benjamin is so called when he was above thirty years (44:20). Solomon called himself a little child when he came to the kingdom ([1 Kings 3:7](/1kgs#1Kgs.3.7)).
